questions.question: Explain how coal formed.
questions.expected_answer: Millions of years ago, plants grew in huge swamps. When they died, they fell into the water, where there was little oxygen, so they did not rot completely and formed peat. The peat was buried under layers of mud and sand. Over millions of years, the weight of the layers and the heat underground squeezed out water and gases and changed the peat into hard, black coal.

questions.question: How did oil and natural gas form, and name three products made from crude oil.
questions.expected_answer: Tiny plants and animals in the sea died and sank to the sea floor, where they were buried in mud with little oxygen. Over millions of years, heat and pressure changed their remains into crude oil and natural gas, which became trapped under rock. Products from crude oil include petrol, diesel, paraffin, jet fuel, machine oil and materials for plastics.

questions.question: Why are fossil fuels non-renewable, and what problems does burning them cause?
questions.expected_answer: They took millions of years to form, but we are using them up in a few hundred years, so they cannot be replaced in a human lifetime and will run out. Burning them releases smoke, ash and harmful gases that pollute the air and harm our lungs, and carbon dioxide, which traps heat and causes climate change. Mining also damages land and water.
